To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Canadian students had higher scores on health responsibility, nutrition, physical activity, spiritual growth, and interpersonal relations than did Jordanian students.

the Jordanian students had a significantly lower score on three of the five HPLP-II subscales (health responsibility, physical activity and interpersonal relations), while the Canadian students had a significantly higher score on the spiritual growth subscale.

the Jordanian and Canadian students had similar scores on all subscales except for the three subscales: (1) health responsibility (Jordanians scored higher); (2) physical activity (Canadian scored higher); (3) interpersonal relations (Canadian scored higher).
In summary, our research is concerned with
health practices of nursing students.
the health-promoting practices among nursing students in Canada and Jordan.
the health status of students and the need to improve their health-promoting lifestyle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the health practices of nursing students from both countries were not adequate and that there is a need to improve the health practices of both groups.
the health-promoting lifestyle of nursing students in both countries is low.
Jordanian nursing students had a lower health-promoting lifestyle than their Canadian counterparts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that Jordanian nursing students are less likely than Canadian students to engage in health-promoting behaviors.
the health practices of the Jordanian nursing students are similar to the health practices of Canadian nursing students.

Jordanian nursing students are more likely to have healthier lifestyles than their Canadian counterparts, and that Jordanian nursing educators need to focus on health-promotion programs and activities for their students.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nursing education is the key to health promotion and that the nursing curricula should be revised to include more health promotion content.
health-promoting lifestyle practices can be enhanced by nursing students in both countries.
nursing education programs need to include health promotion activities and programs in the curriculum.
